gaps.sentence: The government plans to ___ taxes next year.
gaps.hint: the verb takes an object: taxes
gaps.explanation: 'Raise' means to lift or increase something (takes an object); 'rise' means to go up (no object).

gaps.sentence: She wore ___ heels to the party.
gaps.explanation: 'High heels' is the fixed collocation; 'tall' is used for people, buildings and trees.

gaps.hint: you ___ a match, but ___ the other team
gaps.explanation: 'Win' takes the game or prize as object (win a match); 'beat/defeat' take the opponent as object.
'Your' shows possession; 'you're' means 'you are'; 'yours' is a possessive pronoun standing alone.

gaps.hint: past participle after 'have'; the verb takes no object
gaps.explanation: 'Rise' (rise, rose, risen) takes no object: sales have risen. 'Raise' takes an object: they raised prices.

gaps.sentence: Tax is calculated on your total annual ___.
gaps.hint: all the money you receive from every source
gaps.explanation: 'Income' is all the money you receive from work, investments, rent and so on during a period.

gaps.sentence: The bank agreed to ___ him the money.
gaps.hint: meaning: give temporarily (from the giver's point of view)
gaps.explanation: 'Lend' means to give something to someone temporarily; the bank lends money. A base verb is needed after 'to'.
